builders.angle: LITERAL -- the angle that won rounds 20, 23-25 and 29. Work BRIEF-r31's fix list 1 to 3 in order and exactly as written, one wing at a time, the Passages FIRST (the lowest-scored room in the house). Keep every change inside your four wings.

THE NEAR FLOOR FIRST -- both judges' shared defect. Build the dressed, lit near floor (a rug or flags, a pool of lamplight, a prop or two above the hand's edge) as ONE rule your four wings use, prove it there, then sweep all seventeen SEEDED and keep it only where it lifts a room; then each wing's own defect in that light.

THE OBJECT DRAWN, NOT TILED. Each wing's worst thing is a material that reads as a texture: the maze's scallop tile, the passage's soft panels, the kitchen's tangled tables, the chapel's scan-lined gable. Draw each as a real object with crisp inked edges first -- clipped hedge, panelled wainscot, a table with benches, coursed masonry -- then dress and light the near floor.
